summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for evaluation of epigastric pain three months after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass surgery. She reported nausea, one episode of non-bloody vomiting, and looser stools. A CT scan revealed oral contrast in both the gastric pouch and remnant stomach, suggesting a fistulous connection, along with mild dilatation of the proximal efferent limb. An EGD confirmed two perianastomotic ulcers on the jejunal side with no active bleeding, and an H. pylori serology test was negative. She was managed with IV Protonix and pain control using IV morphine, later transitioned to oral omeprazole and Roxicet. Her diet was advanced from clear liquids to bariatric stage III, with a switch to lactose-free to address diarrhea. She tolerated oral intake and medications well, with controlled pain and stable vitals, leading to discharge home with follow-up instructions and a two-week surgical clinic appointment.
problems: Gastrojejunal ulcer, unspecified as acute or chronic, without mention of hemorrhage or perforation, without mention of obstruction
